title: Was Malmstrom incident caused by UFOs warping space and time?
excerpt: Physicist Kevin Knuth explains how one theory on UFO movement could explain how missiles were shut down during a sighting.
content:
A man scours the night sky with binoculars and camera equipment from the Rock of Dunamase in Co Laois. (Niall Carson, PA Images via Getty Images)

(NewsNation) — A physics professor says an Air Force veteran told him about UFOs shutting down intercontinental ballistic missiles at Malmstrom Air Force Base more than once.

Kevin Knuth, the University at Albany SUNY physicist and former NASA Ames researcher, joined NewsNation’s Ross Coulthart to discuss the unexplained incidents.

What’s known as the Malmstrom UFO incident happened in March of 1967. Whistleblower Robert Salas later came forward to talk about a sighting of UFOs over the Montana base, which houses ICBMS.

According to Salas, the missiles mysteriously shut down, which the Pentagon said in 2025 was actually caused by a secret test of an electromagnetic pulse device.

Knuth said he first heard about the Malmstrom incident from a professor.

“At the time we thought that was funny, because that’s hard to believe, that the entire U.S. Air Force wouldn’t be on red alert if that were to happen,” he said.

Later, Knuth was speaking to a relative of his wife’s, who had happened to serve in the Air Force and had been stationed at Malmstrom.

“He goes, oh that used to happen all the time, like it was nothing: ‘Yeah, they’d fly in, they’d shut down all kinds of missiles,'” Knuth recounted.

He offered a possible scientific explanation for how UFOs could accomplish that task, offering one of the theories on how UFOs move.

“They might be warping space in some way, because they’re accelerating at incredibly high rates that otherwise the inertia would kill anybody inside,” Knuth explained.

Missiles are housed in silos deep underground and are constantly running navigation systems so they can be launched at a moment’s notice.

“But if you start messing space and time, you’re going to mess up the navigation system,” Knuth said. “I don’t think they were trying to shut down the missiles, I think it was an accident.”
